coverage_note: The sections where time-consciousness carries the argument: Part 2 §§ 18 and 30, Part 3 § 56, and Supplementary Texts Section 1 (the 1920/21 first version). The remaining 38 sections with term hits, including the affection and association analyses of Part 2, are not extracted.

units.claim: Every intuition leaves an empty presentation that is a retention, and the continual retentional modification of each primordially impressional Now-phase is called the first aspect of the fundamental lawfulness of original time-consciousness.
units.quote: every such empty presentation is a retention, and its necessary connection to past intentions characterizes a fundamental law of passive genesis. This extends into every intuition itself: every Now-phase arising primordially-impressionally is continually modified in retention—the first aspect of fundamental lawfulness of original time-consciousness.

units.claim: Protention is the second aspect of genetic primordial lawfulness, and the protentional and retentional continuities are distinguished by the direction the egoic regard must take in each.
units.quote: Alongside retentions, there are protentions: the second aspect of genetic primordial lawfulness. Just as a retentional horizon is invariably connected to each impressional present, so is a protentional horizon.

units.claim: Brentano is said to be phenomenologically incorrect in calling the connection of retentions to impressions original association, since the synthesis proper to original time-consciousness is not associative.
units.quote: Therefore Brentano was phenomenologically incorrect to characterize the connection of retentions to impressions as "original association." Association is only at work in the protentional path of time-constitution, alongside the continual retentional path.

units.claim: Retentions can take on intentional character only later, through subsequent association, so that the distinction between mere retentions prior to association and their intentional shape is fundamental.
units.quote: The distinction between mere retentions prior to association and their intentional shape is fundamental.

units.claim: Time and space are made principles of individuation: objects uniform in all material respects are individuated by their unique temporal locus, temporal shape being distinguished from temporal identity.
units.quote: Even objects uniform in all material respects are individuated by their different temporal positions. Time and space (for the visual field) are *principia individuationis*—the forms of possible individuality of objects given in the living present.

units.claim: The a-temporality of the judicative proposition is itself declared a distinctive shape of temporality, omni-temporality, so that supra-temporality is a supra-temporal unity found in the temporal manifold.
units.quote: The a-temporality of judgments is itself a distinctive shape of temporality: *omni-temporality*.

units.claim: The original core of the judgment's being is a being in the form of temporality but not the being of an individuum, and the difference between individual and ideal temporal being is called fundamental.
units.quote: The original core of judgment's being is a being in the form of temporality—but not the being of an *individuum*. The difference between individual and ideal temporal being is fundamental.

units.claim: The 1920/21 first version already lays out the typology of presentations - perception, retention, protention, remembering, expectation, co-presentification - each with its temporal orientation.
units.quote: Husserl lays out the basic typology of presentations: perception, retention, protention, remembering, expectation, co-presentification—each with its distinctive temporal orientation and mode of giving its object.

units.claim: The 1920/21 version analyses retention, empty expectation and presentifications of what is temporally present as necessary components of perceptual lived-experience.
units.quote: Husserl analyzes the various forms of presentification (Vergegenwärtigung) as necessary components of perceptual lived-experience: concrete retention and its modalization, empty concrete expectation and its modalization, and concrete empty presentifications of what is temporally present.
